definition: Share of the civilian noninstitutionalized population covered by Medicaid, Medical Assistance or another government plan for people with low income or a disability, alone or with other coverage.
limitations: Survey-reported coverage at time of interview; not an administrative enrollment count Age groups changed in the 2013-2017 release (under 19 instead of under 18); totals for all ages are unaffected.

label: Uninsured rate under 65, annual estimates
sentence_label: annual uninsured rate for people under 65
definition: Model-based estimate of the share of people under 65 without health insurance coverage in a single year.
breaks: The estimates use American Community Survey inputs from 2008; earlier years are not comparable and are not shown.
limitations: Aggregate as sum(NUI_PT)/sum(NIPR_PT); aggregated MOEs are approximate; ages 65+ not covered

label: Uninsured rate under 65 with low income, annual estimates
sentence_label: annual uninsured rate for people under 65 with income at or below 138% of poverty
definition: Model-based estimate of the share of people under 65 with income at or below 138% of the poverty level who have no health insurance coverage in a single year.
universe: Population under 65 with income at or below 138% of poverty
breaks: The estimates use American Community Survey inputs from 2008; earlier years are not comparable and are not shown.
limitations: Wider intervals than all-income estimates; 138% threshold relates to Medicaid expansion eligibility; race detail only for states

label: Current lack of health insurance among adults 18-64 (PLACES)
definition: Model-based percentage of adults aged 18-64 reporting no current health insurance (BRFSS), crude and age-adjusted
table_or_series: PLACES 2025 release (Socrata swc5-untb county; eav7-hnsx place; cwsq-ngmh tract; qnzd-25i4 ZCTA)
comparable_span: Single release only (CDC: model cannot track local change over time)
breaks: 2024 release: 2020 Census geography and CT planning regions; 2023 release: CI simulation change
suppression: Population under 50 suppressed; KY and PA missing in 2025 release (BRFSS 2023)
limitations: Not implemented: the universe (adults 18-64) is not published with the estimates, so combined areas and states cannot be computed; ACS and SAHIE measure coverage directly. Prefer ACS or SAHIE for insurance levels; PLACES useful for tract and ZCTA patterns

label: Primary care Health Professional Shortage Area designation and score (HRSA)
definition: Whether an area (county, county subdivision or census tract component) or facility is covered by a designated primary care HPSA, and its HPSA score (higher = greater shortage; observed 0-25); types: geographic, high-needs geographic, population (e.g., low-income) and facility
variables: HPSA ID;HPSA Status;Designation Type;HPSA Score;HPSA Component Type Description;HPSA Geography Identification Number;HPSA Designation Population;HPSA FTE;HPSA Formal Ratio;Rural Status;HPSA Designation Date;Withdrawn Date
universe: Primary care HPSA designations and their components
periods: Current status (daily file); designation and withdrawal dates allow history reconstruction
breaks: Status 'No Data Provided' appears only in pre-August 2014 records
limitations: Filter HPSA Status = Designated (optionally Proposed For Withdrawal); population HPSAs cover subgroups only; overlapping designations possible; administrative, not a need estimate

label: Mental health Health Professional Shortage Area designation and score (HRSA)
definition: Whether an area or facility is covered by a designated mental health HPSA, and its HPSA score (higher = greater shortage)
variables: HPSA ID;HPSA Status;Designation Type;HPSA Score;HPSA Component Type Description;HPSA Geography Identification Number;HPSA Designation Population;Rural Status
universe: Mental health HPSA designations and their components
breaks: Status 'No Data Provided' appears only in pre-August 2014 records
limitations: Administrative designation, not a need estimate; population HPSAs cover subgroups only

label: Dental health Health Professional Shortage Area designation and score (HRSA)
definition: Whether an area or facility is covered by a designated dental health HPSA, and its HPSA score (higher = greater shortage)
variables: HPSA ID;HPSA Status;Designation Type;HPSA Score;HPSA Component Type Description;HPSA Geography Identification Number;HPSA Designation Population;Rural Status
universe: Dental HPSA designations and their components
breaks: Status 'No Data Provided' appears only in pre-August 2014 records
limitations: Administrative designation; population HPSAs cover subgroups only

label: Medically Underserved Area/Population designation and IMU score (HRSA)
definition: Whether an area (county, county subdivision or tract component) is in a designated MUA or MUP, with Index of Medical Underservice score (0 = highest need to 100; 62.0 or less qualifies; governor designations have no score)
variables: MUA/P ID;MUA/P Status Description;Designation Type;IMU Score;Medically Underserved Area/Population (MUA/P) Component Geographic Type Description;State and County Federal Information Processing Standard Code;County Subdivision FIPS Code;Census Tract;Designation Date;Rural Status Description
periods: Current status (daily file); designations dating back to at least 1994
breaks: IMU scores reflect data at designation or update time
limitations: Score applies to the whole MUA/P; MUPs cover specific populations; administrative, not a current need estimate

label: HRSA health center and look-alike service sites (count)
definition: Number of active service delivery sites of HRSA Health Center Program awardees (FQHCs) and FQHC Look-Alikes located in the area, optionally by location type (permanent, seasonal, mobile van)
variables: Health Center Type;Health Center Location Type Description;Site Status Description;Geocoding Artifact Address Primary X Coordinate;Geocoding Artifact Address Primary Y Coordinate;State and County Federal Information Processing Standard Code;Site Postal Code;Operating Hours per Week
universe: Active health center service delivery sites
suppression: Street address and ZIP suppressed for domestic violence shelter sites
limitations: Counts sites, not capacity or patients; trends require archived snapshots

label: Primary care physicians per 100,000 residents (AHRF)
definition: Non-federal primary care physicians (MD and DO) in patient care, excluding residents, per 100,000 residents; numerator from AHRF (AMA Physician Masterfile), denominator from county population
periods: 2022 and 2023 in the 2024-2025 AHRF; earlier years in prior releases
comparable_span: Within the AHRF series, checking definitions per release
breaks: Variable names change each release; Connecticut planning regions added alongside legacy counties
limitations: Headcounts by county, not FTE; label inferred from AHRF variable name (confirm in technical documentation); CHR&R v004 uses the same AHRF/AMA source

label: Dentists per 100,000 residents (AHRF, NPI-based)
definition: Dentists with a National Provider Identifier located in the county per 100,000 residents
breaks: Variable names change each release
limitations: Counts NPI holders by location, not practicing FTE; label inferred from AHRF variable name (confirm in technical documentation)

label: Medicare-registered hospitals (count, CMS)
definition: Number of Medicare-registered hospitals located in the area, optionally by hospital type (acute care, critical access, psychiatric, children's, rural emergency, VA, DoD) and emergency services
table_or_series: Hospital General Information (Provider Data Catalog xubh-q36u)
limitations: No FIPS or coordinates (join on county name and state, or geocode addresses); counts facilities, not beds or capacity

label: Hospital overall star rating (CMS)
definition: CMS Overall Hospital Quality Star Rating (1-5) summarizing quality measures reported on Care Compare, per hospital
table_or_series: Hospital General Information (Provider Data Catalog xubh-q36u)
universe: Medicare-registered hospitals with enough reported measures
suppression: 'Not Available' for 2,245 of 5,419 hospitals in the August 2026 file (including 983 critical access and all psychiatric hospitals)
limitations: Facility attribute, not an area measure; do not average across hospitals without care

label: Adults with a routine checkup in the past year
sentence_label: share of adults with a routine checkup in the past year
definition: Estimated share of adults who report a routine checkup with a doctor (such as a general physical exam) in the past year.
table_or_series: PLACES 2025 release: county, place, census tract and ZCTA estimates
variables: measureid=CHECKUP; datavaluetypeid=CrdPrv; data_value; low_confidence_limit; high_confidence_limit; totalpop18plus
periods: 2023 survey data (2025 release); latest release only
comparable_span: Latest release only (CDC: the model cannot track local change over time)
breaks: Model-based estimates for adults from CDC's latest PLACES release; CDC advises against comparing releases to measure change. Values are not age-adjusted, so differences between areas partly reflect age.
suppression: Areas with fewer than 50 people are suppressed; Kentucky and Pennsylvania lack the 2023 measures in the 2025 release
limitations: Crude prevalence (CrdPrv). The 95% interval is converted to a 90% MOE (half its width x 1.645/1.96; intervals can be asymmetric). Combined areas and states are sum(prevalence x totalpop18plus)/sum(totalpop18plus), CDC's method for groups of areas, without a MOE; a state needs every county in the table (counties under 50 people are suppressed and left out). The national value is the United States row of the county table (method not documented; e.g. short sleep 36.0% versus 36.1% summed from counties). Not for program evaluation.

label: Premature death: years of potential life lost before 75 (CHR&R)
definition: Years of potential life lost before age 75 per 100,000 population, age-adjusted, from 3 years of NCHS death data (2025 release: 2020-2022)
comparable_span: Trends file across releases; overlapping 3-year windows
breaks: Population-estimate method changes for data years 2004-2006 and 2019-2021
limitations: Overlapping pooled years are not independent; CHR&R terms restrict commercial use

label: Life expectancy at birth (CHR&R)
definition: Average number of years a person can expect to live, from 3 years of NCHS mortality data (2025 release: 2020-2022)
periods: Recent annual releases through 2025 (earliest release not verified)
breaks: Population-estimate method change for data years 2019-2021
suppression: Flags for unreliable or suppressed values
limitations: 2020-2022 window includes COVID-19 years; CHR&R terms restrict commercial use

label: Life expectancy at birth by census tract, 2010-2015 (USALEEP)
definition: Tract life expectancy at birth from abridged period life tables for 2010-2015, with standard error and a flag for observed or predicted age-specific death rates
breaks: 2010 tract boundaries (crosswalk needed for 2020 tracts)
suppression: No estimates for Maine, Wisconsin and tracts with insufficient data (65,662 tracts estimated)
limitations: Dated; large standard errors for small tracts; predicted rates for some age groups

label: All-cause age-adjusted death rate (CDC WONDER)
definition: Deaths from all causes per 100,000 residents, age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population (WONDER default), by county, state or nation of residence; cause-specific rates available via ICD-10 groupings
table_or_series: WONDER Underlying Cause of Death 2018-2024 single race (1999-2020 bridged race for earlier years)
variables: Deaths;Population;Crude Rate;Age Adjusted Rate and 95% CI (query output measures)
comparable_span: 1999-2024 for all-cause totals (race detail changes in 2018)
breaks: ICD-10 from 1999; single-race categories from 2018; unreliable-rate rule changed with 2024 data; Connecticut county rates unavailable 2022 and later
suppression: Counts 1-9 suppressed; rates for 0-9 deaths suppressed; rates hidden when 95% CI width exceeds 160% of the rate
limitations: County export only via the web form; pool years for small counties; 95% CI reflects random variation (not a model), placed under model_interval for lack of a better code

label: Drug overdose deaths, 12-month ending, provisional (NCHS VSRR)
definition: Provisional count of drug overdose deaths among county residents in the 12 months ending in the reference month
table_or_series: VSRR Provisional County-Level Drug Overdose Death Counts (Socrata gb4e-yj24)
breaks: Provisional counts revised as records arrive
limitations: Counts only (compute rates with population); sums across counties omit suppressed cells; pending investigations understate recent counts

label: Drug overdose death rate (CDC injury dashboard)
definition: Deaths from unintentional or undetermined-intent drug overdose per 100,000 residents, annual or trailing twelve months; Bayesian-modeled rate when 1-9 deaths
table_or_series: Mapping Injury, Overdose, and Violence - County (Socrata psx4-wq38)
breaks: Mix of provisional and final data; modeled rates for 1-9 deaths
suppression: Counts under 10 shown as 1-9; unstable modeled rates suppressed
limitations: No age adjustment stated; modeled rates (rate_m = 1) carry credible intervals and cannot be re-aggregated

label: Suicide death rate (CDC injury dashboard)
definition: Deaths from suicide by any method per 100,000 residents, annual or trailing twelve months; Bayesian-modeled rate when 1-9 deaths
table_or_series: Mapping Injury, Overdose, and Violence - County (Socrata psx4-wq38)
breaks: Mix of provisional and final data; modeled rates for 1-9 deaths
suppression: Counts under 10 shown as 1-9; unstable modeled rates suppressed
limitations: No age adjustment stated; small counties mostly modeled; firearm suicide available as FA_Suicide

label: Low-income, low-access tract: SNAP retailers at 1 mile urban / 10 miles rural, straight-line (FARA SRAM)
definition: Flag (1/0) for a low-income census tract that ERS classifies as low access because residents live beyond 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) straight-line distance from the nearest SNAP-authorized retailer (farmers markets and delivery routes excluded); variants at 0.5/10 and 1/20 miles and a vehicle-access version
comparable_span: Single year; not comparable with LRAM
breaks: New July 2026 method differs from LRAM (store universe, gridded population, driving option)
limitations: To summarize areas, count flagged tracts or sum their population rather than averaging flags; proximity only

label: Low-income, low-access tract: SNAP retailers at 1 mile urban / 10 miles rural, driving distance (FARA SRAM)
definition: Same as the straight-line LILA flag but using road-network driving distance to the nearest SNAP-authorized retailer
comparable_span: Single year; driving-distance measures are new in 2026
breaks: First FARA release with driving distance
suppression: Blank when unavailable; 101 stores (97 in Alaska) excluded from driving calculations
limitations: Depends on road-network quality; assumes car travel (no transit or walking)

label: Population far from any SNAP-authorized retailer, 1 mile urban / 10 miles rural (FARA SRAM)
definition: Share of tract population living beyond 1 mile (urban tracts) or 10 miles (rural tracts) straight-line from the nearest SNAP-authorized retailer: SD_SRAM_LAPOP1_10 / POP2020 (driving version uses DD_SRAM_LAPOP1_10)
table_or_series: SRAM Straight Line Distance Data.csv; SRAM Driving Distance Data.csv; SRAM General Tract Characteristics Data.csv
universe: Tract population (2020 Census, distributed with LandScan grid)
breaks: Not comparable with LRAM low-access counts (different store universe and methods)
limitations: Sum counts across tracts before dividing; subgroup counts for low-income, children, seniors, no-vehicle and SNAP households; general characteristics file drops the tract ID leading zero

label: Low-income, low-access tract: supermarkets at 1 mile urban / 10 miles rural (FARA LRAM)
definition: Flag (1/0) for a low-income tract where residents live beyond 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) from the nearest supermarket, supercenter or large grocery store (STARS and TDLinx directories), straight-line distance
table_or_series: 2019 LRAM file Food Access Research Atlas.csv (archived 2015 and 2010 files)
breaks: Replaced by SRAM as the current map in July 2026; 2006 Food Desert Locator used 2000 tracts
limitations: Excludes smaller grocers, dollar and convenience stores (ERS notes this may overstate low access); 2010 tract geography; population from 2010 Census

label: Population with low access to a supermarket or large grocery store, county (Food Environment Atlas)
definition: Percentage of county population living more than 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) from a supermarket, supercenter or large grocery store, aggregated from the LRAM tract analysis
breaks: Not comparable with 2025 SRAM measures
limitations: Supermarket-based definition (LRAM); 2010 population base

label: Adults experiencing food insecurity
sentence_label: share of adults experiencing food insecurity
definition: Estimated share of adults who report that in the past 12 months the food they bought always, usually or sometimes did not last and they did not have money to get more.
table_or_series: PLACES 2025 release: county, place, census tract and ZCTA estimates
variables: measureid=FOODINSECU; datavaluetypeid=CrdPrv; data_value; low_confidence_limit; high_confidence_limit; totalpop18plus
periods: 2023 survey data (2025 release); latest release only
comparable_span: Latest release only (CDC: the model cannot track local change over time)
breaks: Model-based estimates for adults from CDC's latest PLACES release; CDC advises against comparing releases to measure change. Values are not age-adjusted, so differences between areas partly reflect age. These questions were asked only in states that chose to use the survey's optional social needs module.
suppression: Areas with fewer than 50 people are suppressed; Kentucky and Pennsylvania lack the 2023 measures in the 2025 release; social needs measures only for states that used the module
limitations: Crude prevalence (CrdPrv). The 95% interval is converted to a 90% MOE (half its width x 1.645/1.96; intervals can be asymmetric). Combined areas and states are sum(prevalence x totalpop18plus)/sum(totalpop18plus), CDC's method for groups of areas, without a MOE; a state needs every county in the table (counties under 50 people are suppressed and left out). The national value is the United States row of the county table (method not documented; e.g. short sleep 36.0% versus 36.1% summed from counties). Not for program evaluation.

label: Child food insecurity rate (Map the Meal Gap)
definition: Model-based percentage of children living in food-insecure households, using the MMG model with household-with-children predictors
table_or_series: Map the Meal Gap 2026 release (2024 data)
breaks: Same model changes as the overall rate
limitations: Dataset requires request form; variable names not verified; future updates depend on CPS food security data after USDA ended its annual report

label: Grocery stores per 1,000 residents (Food Environment Atlas)
definition: Supermarkets and smaller grocery stores (County Business Patterns NAICS 445110 establishments) per 1,000 county residents
breaks: Each Atlas version re-bases years
limitations: Establishment counts, not store size, prices or quality

label: SNAP-authorized stores per 1,000 residents (Food Environment Atlas)
definition: Average monthly number of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits per 1,000 county residents (FNA data)
breaks: Each Atlas version re-bases years
limitations: Includes all SNAP store types (convenience stores were 47% of active retailers in FNA data at end of 2025)

label: Fast-food restaurants per 1,000 residents (Food Environment Atlas)
definition: Limited-service restaurants (County Business Patterns NAICS 722513) per 1,000 county residents
breaks: Each Atlas version re-bases years
limitations: Establishment location, not customers; per-resident rates run high where outlets serve visitors or commuters

label: Convenience stores per 1,000 residents (Food Environment Atlas)
definition: Convenience stores and gas stations with convenience stores (County Business Patterns NAICS 445120, 447110) per 1,000 county residents
breaks: Each Atlas version re-bases years
limitations: Establishment counts only

label: SNAP-authorized retailers (count, FNA retailer data)
definition: Number of SNAP-authorized retailers located in an area on a reference date (authorization date on or before the date and end date blank or later), optionally by store type (e.g., Supermarket, Super Store, Convenience Store)
variables: Record ID;Store Name;Store Type;Latitude;Longitude;State;County;Zip Code;Authorization Date;End Date
periods: Any reference date 2005-2025 (current as of December 31, 2025)
comparable_span: 2005-2025 (early years may miss retailers that ended before the 20-year window)
breaks: Store types are FNA administrative categories
limitations: Exclude Farmers' Market and Delivery Route types for fixed-store access; coordinates can be wrong; authorization does not describe stock or size

label: Food Environment Index (CHR&R)
definition: Index from 0 (worst) to 10 (best) combining limited access to healthy foods (Food Environment Atlas) and food insecurity (Map the Meal Gap)
periods: 2025 release uses 2019 and 2022 inputs; earlier annual releases
breaks: Inputs and years change by release
limitations: Composite of modeled inputs with state effects; CHR&R advises comparing within states; license restricts commercial use

label: Households in poverty receiving SNAP
sentence_label: share of households below the poverty level that received SNAP benefits
definition: Share of households with income below the poverty level in the past 12 months that received SNAP (food stamp) benefits.
periods: 1-year 2005-2024 for areas with 65,000+ people; 5-year periods through 2020-2024
limitations: Not a program participation rate (SNAP eligibility rules differ from the poverty line); survey under-reporting

label: Adults receiving SNAP
sentence_label: share of adults who received SNAP
definition: Estimated share of adults who report receiving SNAP (food stamp) benefits in the past 12 months.
table_or_series: PLACES 2025 release: county, place, census tract and ZCTA estimates
variables: measureid=FOODSTAMP; datavaluetypeid=CrdPrv; data_value; low_confidence_limit; high_confidence_limit; totalpop18plus
periods: 2023 survey data (2025 release); latest release only
comparable_span: Latest release only (CDC: the model cannot track local change over time)
breaks: Model-based estimates for adults from CDC's latest PLACES release; CDC advises against comparing releases to measure change. Values are not age-adjusted, so differences between areas partly reflect age. These questions were asked only in states that chose to use the survey's optional social needs module.
suppression: Areas with fewer than 50 people are suppressed; Kentucky and Pennsylvania lack the 2023 measures in the 2025 release; social needs measures only for states that used the module
limitations: Crude prevalence (CrdPrv). The 95% interval is converted to a 90% MOE (half its width x 1.645/1.96; intervals can be asymmetric). Combined areas and states are sum(prevalence x totalpop18plus)/sum(totalpop18plus), CDC's method for groups of areas, without a MOE; a state needs every county in the table (counties under 50 people are suppressed and left out). The national value is the United States row of the county table (method not documented; e.g. short sleep 36.0% versus 36.1% summed from counties). Not for program evaluation.

label: SNAP participants by county or project area, January and July (FNA)
definition: Number of persons participating in SNAP in the reporting month (public assistance and non-public assistance households combined), by county or SNAP project area
table_or_series: Bi-Annual State Project Area/County Level Participation and Issuance Data (FNS-388A) snap-zip-fns388a-2.zip
variables: Calc: SNAP Total PA and Non-PA People;SNAP All Persons Public Assistance Participation;SNAP All Persons Non-Public Assistance Participation;Calc: SNAP Total PA and Non-PA Households;Substate/Region
comparable_span: Consistent where a state reports by county
limitations: Not all states report by county; substate codes combine state FIPS, county FIPS and office, and statewide rows (e.g., code 999) are not counties; one month, not an annual average

label: SNAP benefit issuance by county or project area, January and July (FNA)
definition: Total SNAP benefits issued in the reporting month (public assistance and non-public assistance) by county or SNAP project area
table_or_series: Bi-Annual State Project Area/County Level Participation and Issuance Data (FNS-388A) snap-zip-fns388a-2.zip
variables: SNAP All Total Actual PA & Non-PA Issuance;Substate/Region
comparable_span: Nominal dollars; adjust for inflation and benefit-rule changes
limitations: Not all states report by county; nominal dollars; may include disaster assistance

label: SNAP participants by state and month (FNA)
definition: Number of persons participating in SNAP by state and month
table_or_series: SNAP state-level tables (snap-persons-9.xlsx; FY files in snap-zip-fy69tocurrent-9.zip)
variables: Persons participating by State/Territory and month
breaks: Recent months preliminary and revised; large 2025-2026 changes in some states (Arizona about -52.5% June 2025 to June 2026 initial)
limitations: Preliminary months subject to significant revision; may include disaster assistance

label: Rental vacancy rate
sentence_label: rental vacancy rate
definition: Vacant units for rent as a share of the rental inventory (renter-occupied units, units for rent, and units rented but not yet occupied).
universe: Rental inventory (renter-occupied plus vacant for rent and rented, not occupied)
breaks: The collection of vacancy status changed in 2013 (ACS subject definitions).
limitations: Small vacant counts give large MOEs in small areas.

label: Homeowner vacancy rate
sentence_label: homeowner vacancy rate
definition: Vacant units for sale as a share of the homeowner inventory (owner-occupied units, units for sale, and units sold but not yet occupied).
universe: Homeowner inventory (owner-occupied plus vacant for sale only and sold, not occupied)
limitations: Usually very small percentages with wide MOEs below county level.

label: Seasonal and recreational homes
sentence_label: share of homes held for seasonal, recreational or occasional use
definition: Vacant units held for seasonal, recreational or occasional use as a share of all housing units.
breaks: The collection of vacancy status changed in 2013 (ACS subject definitions).
limitations: Other vacant (B25004_008) is a separate category often associated with units held off market.

label: Single-family detached homes
sentence_label: share of homes that are single-family detached houses
definition: Housing units in one-unit detached structures as a share of all housing units.

label: Homes in buildings with 5 or more units
sentence_label: share of homes in buildings with 5 or more units
definition: Housing units in structures with 5 or more units as a share of all housing units.
limitations: Mobile home share = B25024_010 / B25024_001.

label: Median year built
sentence_label: median year homes were built
definition: Median year in which housing units' structures were built.
breaks: Year-built categories changed in 2012, 2015 and 2021; the categories are read for each period.
suppression: ACS special values; open-ended bins flagged by median+/- annotations
limitations: Self-reported year built; recompute for aggregates from B25034 bins (approximate).

label: Renters paying 50% or more of income on rent
sentence_label: share of renters paying 50 percent or more of income on rent
definition: Share of renter households (with rent computed as a share of income) paying 50 percent or more of household income on gross rent.
universe: Renter-occupied housing units with computed gross rent as percentage of income
limitations: See renter_cost_burden_30plus_acs.

label: Median rent as a share of income
sentence_label: median gross rent as a share of household income
definition: Median of gross rent as a percentage of past-12-month household income.
universe: Renter-occupied housing units paying cash rent
suppression: ACS special values; open-ended medians flagged by median+/- annotations
limitations: Aggregates only approximable from B25070 bins.

label: Homeowners paying 30% or more of income on housing
sentence_label: share of homeowners spending 30 percent or more of income on housing costs
definition: Share of homeowner households (with costs computed as a share of income) spending 30 percent or more of household income on selected monthly owner costs, with or without a mortgage.
universe: Owner-occupied housing units with computed costs as percentage of income
limitations: Selected monthly owner costs include mortgage, taxes, insurance, utilities and fees.

label: Housing units (decennial census)
definition: Census count of housing units on April 1. Variables by dataset: 2020 DHC H1_001N; 2020 PL H1_001N; 2010 SF1 H001001; 2000 SF1 H001001.
comparable_span: 2000-2020 at state level; substate areas need boundary harmonization
breaks: Each census tabulated on its own boundaries (CT legacy counties in all three); 2020 values subject to disclosure avoidance.
limitations: 2010 and 2000 SF1 are sources census_dec_2010_sf1 and census_dec_2000_sf1.

label: Vacant share of housing units (decennial census)
breaks: Vacancy status categories differ: 2000 has combined 'rented or sold, not occupied' (H005004); 2010/2020 split them (H005003/H005005; H5_003N/H5_005N).

label: Homeownership rate (decennial census)
breaks: 2010 and 2020 split owners into with mortgage/loan and free and clear; 2000 has one owner line; 2020 PL has no tenure.

label: Housing unit estimates (PEP)
definition: Estimated housing units on July 1 each year (with April 1, 2020 base).
variables: V2025 xlsx columns: April 1, 2020 Estimates Base; Housing Unit Estimate (as of July 1) 2020-2025. V2020 CSV: CENSUS2010HU;HUESTIMATESBASE2010;HUESTIMATE2010..HUESTIMATE2020
breaks: Each vintage revises its series; V2020 (2010-based) and V2025 (2020-based) are not a continuous series; CT planning regions in V2025.
limitations: xlsx rows are named, not coded; match names to FIPS carefully.

label: New housing units authorized by building permits (BPS)
definition: Sum of units in 1-unit, 2-unit, 3-4 unit and 5+ unit buildings authorized during the year (estimates with imputation).
variables: County file columns 8, 11, 14, 17 (1-unit, 2-units, 3-4 units, 5+ units Units, imputed); place file columns 19, 22, 25, 28; reported-only units: county 20/23/26/29, place 31/34/37/40
universe: New privately-owned residential units authorized in permit-issuing jurisdictions
breaks: Permit universe reselected 2004 (about 20,000 places), about 20,100 places 2014-2022, annually updated from 2023; place file layouts change 1999, 2003, 2004 and 2007; CT planning regions in county files from 2023.
limitations: Permits are authorizations, not starts or completions; excludes areas without permit systems; places exclude county unincorporated offices (FIPS place 99990).

label: Single-family (1-unit) units authorized (BPS)
definition: Units in 1-unit buildings authorized by permits during the year (estimates with imputation).
variables: County column 8 (1-unit Units); place column 19; reported-only county 20, place 31
breaks: As permitted_units_total_bps.
limitations: Structure-size category '1-unit' as defined by BPS; see documentation for attached-unit treatment.

label: Units in 5+ unit buildings authorized (BPS)
definition: Units in buildings with 5 or more units authorized by permits during the year (estimates with imputation).
variables: County column 17 (5+ units Units); place column 28; reported-only county 29, place 40
universe: New privately-owned residential buildings with 5+ units
breaks: As permitted_units_total_bps.
limitations: Lumpy year to year (single large projects); prefer multi-year sums for small areas.

label: Housing units authorized per 1,000 residents (BPS with PEP)
definition: Total units authorized during the year divided by July 1 resident population (PEP) x 1,000.
table_or_series: BPS county/place annual files; PEP CO-EST2025-ALLDATA / SUB-EST2025
variables: Numerator: BPS total units (see permitted_units_total_bps); denominator: POPESTIMATE{year}
breaks: Population denominators change with vintage; CT counties change 2022/2023.
limitations: Match place permit offices to PEP places via FIPS place (2007+ files); unincorporated remainders need county-level treatment.

label: Annual house price appreciation (FHFA)
definition: Percent change in the annual HPI from the prior year.
universe: Properties with mortgages bought or guaranteed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac
breaks: Revisions; developmental.
limitations: Year-to-year noise in small areas; nominal.

label: House price growth since 2000 (FHFA index, 2000=100)
definition: Annual HPI rebased so that 2000 = 100 (1990-based version also published).
variables: HPI with 2000 base; HPI with 1990 base (xlsx); hpi2000; hpi1990 (tract csv)
universe: Properties with mortgages bought or guaranteed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac
breaks: Blank if the area has no 2000 index value.
limitations: Cumulative nominal appreciation; compare with CPI for real change.

label: Fair Market Rent, 2-bedroom (HUD)
definition: HUD FMR for a 2-bedroom unit: 40th percentile gross rent for standard-quality units in the FMR area containing the county or New England town.
variables: fmr_2 (also fmr_0, fmr_1, fmr_3, fmr_4); keys fips (10-digit), hud_area_code
universe: Standard-quality rental units in the FMR area
comparable_span: Within FMR area across fiscal years
breaks: FMR area redefinitions follow OMB delineations; methodology revisions; FY2026 revised mid-year (effective May 21, 2026).
limitations: Program parameter shared by all counties in an FMR area; not a local market median.

label: Small Area Fair Market Rent, 2-bedroom (HUD)
definition: ZIP-Code-level FMR for a 2-bedroom unit within metropolitan FMR areas.
variables: SAFMR 2BR (also 0BR-4BR and 90%/110% payment standard columns); ZIP Code; HUD Area Code
universe: Rental units in the ZIP Code (metro areas)
breaks: ZIP boundaries change; designated-area list changes.
limitations: USPS ZIP Codes are not ZCTAs; crosswalk needed for Census geographies.

label: Low-income renters with cost burden over 30% (CHAS)
definition: Renter households with income <=80% HAMFI paying more than 30% of income for housing, divided by all such renters with computed burden: (T8_est73+T8_est76+T8_est86+T8_est89+T8_est99+T8_est102) / (T8_est69+T8_est82+T8_est95 - T8_est79 - T8_est92 - T8_est105).
table_or_series: CHAS Table 8 (Tenure by Household Income by Housing Cost Burden by Substandard Housing)
universe: Renter-occupied households with income at or below 80% of HAMFI
breaks: HAMFI thresholds change yearly; recent releases have Census disclosure-avoidance suppression.
suppression: Some cells suppressed by Census (per HUD); MOEs in T8_moe*
limitations: Use T8_moe* columns for error; income limits from HUD, not ACS medians.

label: Extremely low-income renters with severe cost burden (CHAS)
definition: Renter households with income <=30% HAMFI paying more than 50% of income for housing, divided by such renters with computed burden: T8_est76 / (T8_est69 - T8_est79).
universe: Renter-occupied households with income at or below 30% of HAMFI
breaks: As low_income_renters_cost_burdened_chas.
suppression: Some cells suppressed by Census (per HUD)
limitations: Small denominators in small places and tracts.

label: People experiencing homelessness, point-in-time count (HUD PIT)
definition: Sheltered plus unsheltered people counted on a single night in January by the Continuum of Care.
universe: People experiencing homelessness on the count night
breaks: CoC mergers and boundary changes; count methods vary by CoC and year.
limitations: CoC geography only; not a rate; undercount likely, especially unsheltered.

label: Unsheltered homeless people (HUD PIT)
definition: People counted in places not meant for human habitation on the PIT night.
universe: People experiencing homelessness on the count night
breaks: As homeless_total_pit.
limitations: Unsheltered count methods differ by CoC; most sensitive component to method and weather.

label: Sheltered homeless people (HUD PIT)
definition: People in emergency shelter, transitional housing or safe havens on the PIT night.
variables: Sheltered Total Homeless (components: Sheltered ES Homeless; Sheltered TH Homeless; Sheltered SH Homeless)
universe: People experiencing homelessness on the count night
breaks: As homeless_total_pit.
limitations: Depends on shelter capacity (see HIC beds).

label: Chronically homeless people (HUD PIT)
definition: People meeting HUD's chronic homelessness definition counted on the PIT night.
variables: Overall Chronically Homeless (also Sheltered/Unsheltered Chronically Homeless)
universe: People experiencing homelessness on the count night
comparable_span: Check field list sheet for years available
breaks: Field availability and definitions vary by year; check the 'field list, all years' sheet.
limitations: Definition-dependent; verify comparability before trend lines.

label: Homeless people in families with children (HUD PIT)
definition: People in households with at least one adult and one child counted on the PIT night.
variables: Overall Homeless People in Families (also Overall Homeless Family Households)
universe: People experiencing homelessness on the count night
breaks: As homeless_total_pit.
limitations: Family definitions per HUD PIT guidance.

label: Homeless veterans (HUD PIT)
definition: Veterans experiencing homelessness counted on the PIT night.
universe: Adults experiencing homelessness on the count night
breaks: As homeless_total_pit.
limitations: CoC geography only; small counts in rural CoCs.

label: Year-round shelter beds (HUD HIC)
definition: Year-round beds in emergency shelter, transitional housing and safe havens on the HIC night.
variables: Total Year-Round Beds (ES, TH, SH) (also ES, TH, SH components and Dedicated Veteran/Youth Beds)
universe: Homeless assistance projects reporting to the HIC
breaks: Project types and bed categories change across years.
limitations: Inventory, not utilization; seasonal and overflow beds counted separately.

label: Residential address vacancy rate (HUD-USPS)
definition: Residential addresses USPS carriers flag as vacant (not collecting mail for 90+ days on urban routes) divided by all residential addresses x 100.
table_or_series: HUD Aggregated USPS Administrative Data on Address Vacancies (quarterly)
variables: RES_VAC;AMS_RES (Q4 2020 onward layout); pre-Q4 2007 layout uses VAC and AMS
universe: Residential addresses in the USPS Address Management System
breaks: Layout changes Q4 2007 and Q4 2020; dictionary labels GEOID as 2000 Census tract (verify vintage in delivered data).
suppression: Restricted: registered governmental and non-profit users only
limitations: No-stat addresses (e.g., rural vacant, under construction) are separate from vacant.

label: Rental vacancy rate (CPS/HVS)
definition: Share of the rental inventory vacant for rent, from the Current Population Survey/Housing Vacancy Survey.
table_or_series: HVS annual Table 3 (states, 1986-2025); historical Table 1 (U.S. quarterly, 1956-present)
variables: Table 3 annual state rates; Table B-3 MOEs
breaks: Revised series columns (e.g., 1989r1); COVID-19 period collection caution.
suppression: None; MOEs in annual Table B-3
limitations: CPS survey MOEs (not ACS); uncertainty code acs_moe used as closest value. State rates noisy.

label: Homeownership rate (CPS/HVS)
definition: Owner-occupied households as a share of occupied households, from the CPS/HVS.
table_or_series: HVS annual Table 15 (states, 1984-2025); Table 16 (75 largest MSAs, 2015-2025); historical Table 14 (U.S./regions quarterly, 1964-present)
variables: Table 15 annual state rates; Table 16 MSA rates; Table B-3 MOEs
breaks: Series revisions and CPS weighting changes; COVID-19 period caution.
suppression: None; MOEs in annual Table B-3
limitations: Timelier than ACS but noisy for states and MSAs; uncertainty code acs_moe used for CPS MOEs.

label: Eviction filing rate (Eviction Lab, observed)
definition: Eviction filings per 100 renting households, from validated proprietary court-record data.
breaks: Coverage varies by year and state; invalid or low-count observations removed.
limitations: Filings include repeat filings; filings are not completed evictions; ends 2018.

label: Estimated eviction filings, modeled (Eviction Lab)
definition: Model-predicted annual eviction filings with 95% credible intervals for every county.
breaks: Model-based; indicator ind_filings_court_issued shows where court data informed estimates.
limitations: Credible intervals are not additive; Eviction Lab says modeled data are not for multivariate analysis.

label: Resident population, July 1 estimate (PEP)
definition: Estimated resident population on July 1 of each year; April 1, 2020 estimates base.
breaks: Vintage revisions; 4/1/2020 base differs slightly from Census count; CT planning regions from V2022.
limitations: Always use the latest vintage for 2020+; never mix vintages.

label: Annual population change, percent (PEP)
definition: Change in July 1 population from the prior year divided by the prior-year estimate x 100 (NPOPCHG gives the numeric change).
variables: NPOPCHG2021..NPOPCHG2025 (county file; NPOPCHG_2021.. in NST file);POPESTIMATE2020..POPESTIMATE2025
breaks: NPOPCHG2020 covers 4/1/2020-7/1/2020 only (partial year).
limitations: Includes residual component.

label: Natural increase rate (PEP)
definition: Births minus deaths during the July-June year per 1,000 average population.
breaks: Rates not published for the partial 2020 period.
limitations: Rate denominator = average of beginning and ending July 1 populations.

label: Net domestic migration rate (PEP)
definition: Net domestic migration during the July-June year per 1,000 average population.
breaks: Method revisions by vintage.
limitations: Nation's domestic migration is zero by definition.

label: Net international migration rate (PEP)
definition: Net international migration during the July-June year per 1,000 average population (includes native-born, Puerto Rico and Armed Forces movements).
breaks: Check each vintage's release notes for method changes; vintages are not additive.
limitations: County allocation of international migration is modeled.

label: City/town population, July 1 estimate (PEP)
definition: Estimated resident population of incorporated places, consolidated cities and minor civil divisions.
comparable_span: Within vintage; intercensal splices use different boundaries
breaks: Boundaries as of January 1 of each vintage; annexations shift places between vintages.
limitations: No CDP estimates; sum 157 parts for county-within-place detail.

label: Population age 65+, share (PEP)
definition: Population age 65 and over divided by total population x 100.
breaks: Vintage revisions; 2000s files use different layout.
limitations: State totals require summing counties or using state ASRH files.

label: Median age (PEP)
definition: Median age of the resident population.
breaks: Vintage revisions.
limitations: Recompute for aggregates from single-year-of-age (SYASEX) files.

label: Race and Hispanic origin shares (PEP)
definition: Hispanic (H_MALE+H_FEMALE) and non-Hispanic single-race groups (NHWA, NHBA, NHIA, NHAA, NHNA, NHTOM male+female) divided by TOT_POP at AGEGRP 0.
breaks: No Some Other Race category (modified race); differs from Census/ACS race distributions.
limitations: Alone-or-in-combination columns (WAC, BAC, ...) overlap and do not sum to total.

label: Resident population 2010-2019, intercensal (PEP)
definition: Intercensal July 1 population estimates 2010-2019 consistent with the 2010 and 2020 Censuses.
breaks: CT legacy counties (break with V2022+ planning regions); 4/1/2020 value differs slightly from V2025 base.
limitations: Splice with V2025 at 2020; flag the CT county break.

label: Resident population 2000-2009, intercensal (PEP)
definition: Intercensal July 1 population estimates 2000-2009 consistent with the 2000 and 2010 Censuses.
breaks: 2010 county codes (Bedford city, Valdez-Cordova, Shannon, Wade Hampton) differ from 2020 codes.
limitations: co-est00int-tot.csv has unpadded codes; pad STATE to 2 and COUNTY to 3 digits.

label: County population estimates 1970-1999 (PEP historical)
definition: July 1 county population estimates 1970-1999 from historical text files.
variables: Fixed-width year columns (e7079co: 1970 census then 1971-1979 estimates; 99c8: 7/1/1999 back to 7/1/1990 then 4/1/1990 base)
breaks: Different vintages/methods by decade; 1970s rounded to hundreds; county set of each era.
limitations: Custom fixed-width parsing; harmonize county codes before splicing with 2000+ series.

label: Residents under 18
sentence_label: share of residents under 18
definition: Residents under 18 as a share of the total population.
limitations: Summing 8 cells compounds MOE; use approximation formulas.

label: Foreign-born residents
sentence_label: share of residents born abroad
definition: Residents born outside the United States who were not U.S. citizens at birth (naturalized citizens and noncitizens), as a share of the total population.
limitations: Region of birth detail in _015-_020 and _022-_027.

label: Residents who moved in the past year
sentence_label: share of residents who moved in the past year
definition: Residents aged 1 and over who lived in a different home one year earlier (in the same county, elsewhere in the state, in another state or abroad), as a share of residents aged 1 and over.
universe: Population 1 year and over in the United States
limitations: Same house 1 year ago = B07003_004.

label: Residents who speak English less than very well
sentence_label: share of residents 5 and over who speak English less than "very well"
definition: Residents aged 5 and over who speak a language other than English at home and speak English less than "very well", as a share of residents aged 5 and over.
periods: 5-year 2012-2016 to 2020-2024 (C16001 absent from 5-year API metadata before 2016); 1-year 2016-2024 with current lines
breaks: Language categories were redesigned in 2016; earlier periods are not comparable and are not shown.
limitations: Spanish speakers = C16001_003; detailed languages in B16001 (128 lines) have limited geography.

label: Veterans
sentence_label: share of civilian adults who are veterans
definition: Civilian veterans as a share of the civilian population 18 and over.
limitations: Age and sex detail in B21001_004-_039. B21001 had a different layout before the 2006-2010 release (line 002 was Male).

label: Total population (decennial census)
definition: Census count of resident population on April 1. 2020 PL/DHC P1_001N; 2010 SF1 P001001; 2000 SF1 P001001.
breaks: Each census on its own geography; 2020 disclosure avoidance.
limitations: For 1900-1990 county counts use county_population_census_1900_1990.

label: Race and Hispanic origin (decennial census)

breaks: 2020 race and Hispanic origin question design and coding changed (write-ins for White and Black, 200 characters, up to 6 codes, combined code list); Some Other Race and multiracial categories most affected.
limitations: Census cautions that 2020 differences reflect both demographic change and measurement improvements.

label: Median age (decennial census)

breaks: 2020 disclosure avoidance.
limitations: Age detail in P12 (2020 DHC) and P012 (2010/2000 SF1); 2020 PL has only 18+.

label: County population by census, 1900-1990 (Census cencounts)

breaks: County boundary changes not adjusted; later census corrections not reflected; defunct counties use decimal codes.
limitations: Link to 2000+ series by FIPS with care for changed counties.

label: State population by census, 1910-2020

variables: Resident Population;Percent Change in Resident Population;Resident Population Density (by Name, Geography Type, Year)
units: people; percent; people per square mile
breaks: Resident population differs from apportionment population (not used here).
limitations: Numbers stored as quoted strings with commas.

label: Population and rank of the 100 largest urban places, 1790-1990

table_or_series: Working Paper 27 tables tab01-tab26 (tab02-tab22 one census each)
variables: Rank; Population (fixed-width text by place name)
universe: Urban places ranked among the 100 largest
comparable_span: Only while a place is in the top 100
breaks: Place boundaries as of each census; some urban places are towns or townships.
limitations: Name matching to FIPS needed; covers only large places.

label: Households

limitations: Equals occupied housing units (B25002_002) conceptually.

label: Family households
sentence_label: share of households that are families
definition: Family households (a householder living with relatives) as a share of all households.
limitations: Other family, no spouse present = B11001_004 (_005 male, _006 female householder).

label: Married-couple households
sentence_label: share of households that are married-couple families
definition: Married-couple family households as a share of all households.

label: People living alone
sentence_label: share of households with one person living alone
definition: Households of one person living alone as a share of all households.
limitations: Household size distribution in B11016 (1-person = B11016_010).

label: Average household size
sentence_label: average household size
definition: Residents of occupied housing units divided by the number of occupied housing units (households).
limitations: For aggregates compute B25008_001 / B25003_001.

label: Households where grandparents are responsible for grandchildren
sentence_label: share of households where grandparents are responsible for their grandchildren

variables: B10063_003;B10063_001 (also _002 with grandparents living with grandchildren; _004 no parent present)
limitations: Person-level grandparent caregiver counts in B10051.

label: Households (decennial census)
definition: Census count of households. 2020 DHC P16_001N; 2010 SF1 P018001; 2000 SF1 P015001.
breaks: 2020 disclosure avoidance.
limitations: 2020 PL has occupied units (H1_002N) but no household tables.

label: Household type: family, married-couple, living alone (decennial census)

breaks: 2010 labels husband-wife family; 2020 married couple family (includes same-sex spouses).
limitations: 2000 SF1 equivalent not verified here.

label: Average household size (decennial census)
definition: Persons per household. 2010 SF1 P017001; 2000 SF1 P017001; 2020 DHC computed as P15_001N (population in households) / P16_001N (households).
breaks: 2020 value must be computed (no single published cell found).

periods: 2023 survey data (2025 release); latest release only

Counts establishments with paid employees and their employees where they are located; excludes self-employed people, private household employees, railroad employees, crop and animal production and most government employees.
suppression: From 2007 values are published with noise; before 2017 the employment and payroll of small cells were withheld (shown as suppressed); from 2017 cells with fewer than 3 establishments are not published (suppressed).
limitations: Counts establishments with paid employees and their employees where they are located; excludes self-employed people, private household employees, railroad employees, crop and animal production and most government employees. Census Data API {year}/cbp with EMPSZES=001 and (from 2008) LFO=001.
